title: Lawful basis for data collection
description: Collection of government ID and six-digit codes may lack clear lawful basis under applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Sensitive data (passwords, government ID) transmitted from parent to authentication service may be intercepted or modified during transmission.

title: Insufficient notice of data collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what data is being collected, why, and how it will be used during registration.

title: Excessive data collection
description: Collection of government ID and six-digit codes may exceed what is necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles.

title: Inadequate data destruction
description: Personal data collected during registration may not be securely destroyed when no longer needed, increasing risk of exposure.

title: Data uniqueness and re-identification
description: Government ID combined with other personal data may enable unique identification of individuals, increasing privacy risk.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Authentication service may not be fully compliant with applicable privacy regulations regarding data collection, storage, and processing.

title: Data Integrity - Unauthorized Modification of Parent Account Information
description: Parent account information stored in MongoDB could be modified, corrupted, or tampered with by unauthorized actors, potentially compromising authentication credentials and account security.
assumptions: MongoDB database is accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Data Accuracy - Incorrect Parent Account Information Storage
description: Parent account information may be entered incorrectly during authentication service operation, leading to authentication failures or incorrect account associations.
assumptions: User input validation is not comprehensive

title: Data Availability - MongoDB Downtime Affecting Authentication
description: MongoDB database could experience downtime or performance issues, preventing authentication service from storing parent account information and potentially blocking legitimate user access.
assumptions: MongoDB infrastructure is reliable and monitored

title: Data Retention - Excessive Parent Account Information Storage Duration
description: Parent account information may be retained longer than necessary for authentication purposes, increasing exposure to data breaches and privacy risks.
assumptions: No defined data retention policy exists

title: Notification - Users Not Informed About Parent Account Data Storage
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what parent account information is being stored, why it is stored, and how it will be used, violating transparency requirements.
assumptions: Privacy policy does not clearly communicate data storage practices

title: Unauthorized Access to JWT Token
description: JWT tokens transmitted from Authentication Service to Parent User may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially leading to identity theft or account compromise.

title: Disclosure of User Data
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may be exposed if not properly encrypted or protected during transmission, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.

title: Information Leakage via JWT
description: JWT may contain sensitive user information that could be leaked if the token structure or payload is not properly secured, potentially exposing user identity or preferences.

title: Non-compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Transmission of user data and JWT may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper security measures and consent mechanisms are not in place.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Authentication Credentials
description: Parent email and password may be intercepted or leaked during transmission to Authentication Service, potentially exposing child's identity and access credentials to unauthorized parties.

title: Lack of Control Over Personal Information
description: Child user has limited control over the personal information (parent email, password) being collected and processed during authentication, potentially leading to unintended data sharing.

title: Insufficient Notification of Data Collection
description: Child user may not be adequately notified about what information is being collected, how it will be used, or with whom it will be shared during the authentication process.

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Authentication Information
description: Parent email or password information may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, potentially leading to authentication failures or security vulnerabilities.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: Authentication process may not comply with child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K), potentially resulting in legal and regulatory violations.

title: JWT Token Leakage During Transmission
description: JWT tokens containing child user information may be intercepted during transmission from Authentication Service to Child User, potentially exposing sensitive user data.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Child Profiles
description: Child profile information transmitted with JWT may be disclosed to unauthorized parties or in unintended contexts during the authentication flow.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profiles
description: Child User may have unauthorized access to their own profile information or may be targeted by attackers to access profiles of other children.

title: Excessive Identifiers in Child Profiles
description: Child profiles may contain excessive personal identifiers that increase privacy risk and reduce anonymization effectiveness.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile information (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties during transmission or storage, potentially exposing sensitive personal data of minors.

title: Inaccurate Child Profile Information
description: Child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) may contain errors or be entered incorrectly, leading to inaccurate records that could affect the child's identity, benefits, or legal status.

title: Non-compliance with Child Privacy Laws
description: Collection of child personal data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K), potentially resulting in legal penalties and loss of trust.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Process may collect more child profile data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy risk.

title: Lack of Privacy Notice
description: Parent User may not receive adequate notice about how child profile data will be collected, used, stored, and shared, violating transparency requirements.

title: Unauthorized Deletion of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data may be deleted or modified without proper authorization, potentially removing critical information about children.
assumptions: Assumes there are no proper access controls or audit mechanisms in place for profile deletion operations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Profile Information
description: Child profile data may be accessed by unauthorized individuals, including unauthorized staff or external parties, compromising child privacy.
assumptions: Assumes there are insufficient access controls or authentication mechanisms protecting the childprofiles collection.

title: Lack of Control Over Child Profile Updates
description: There may be insufficient controls over who can update child profile information, leading to potential data manipulation or unauthorized changes.
assumptions: Assumes there are no proper role-based access controls or approval workflows for profile updates.

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: Child profile management may not comply with applicable regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes the system may not have proper compliance mechanisms for child-specific data protection requirements.

title: Data Integrity Compromise in MongoDB Collection
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with without proper integrity controls.
assumptions: Assumes there are no database-level integrity constraints or audit mechanisms for the childprofiles collection.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Child User Search History
description: Child user's video search history and interaction data may be disclosed to other users, advertisers, or third parties without explicit consent, violating child privacy expectations.

title: Lack of Control Over Personal Data Usage
description: Child users may not have meaningful control over how their search history, likes, and comments are used for profiling, advertising, or data sharing with third parties.

title: Inaccurate Recording of User Interactions
description: The system may fail to accurately capture or record child user interactions (likes, comments, searches), leading to incomplete or incorrect user profiles.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Privacy Regulations
description: The video management service may not comply with COPPA or other child privacy regulations regarding collection, use, and disclosure of personal information from children.

title: Poor Data Quality in User Interaction Records
description: The video management service may collect incomplete or inaccurate data about child user interactions, affecting the quality of personalized recommendations and user experience.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Files
description: Video files and metadata stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized users if authentication and authorization controls are insufficient.

title: Lack of User Control Over Video Data
description: Users may not have adequate control to manage their video data, including deletion, access permissions, and data portability.

title: Video Data Corruption During Storage
description: Video files and metadata stored in MongoDB could be corrupted during storage operations, leading to data integrity issues.

title: Inaccurate Video Metadata
description: Video metadata stored in the system could be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, affecting data quality and user experience.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Video data handling may not comply with applicable privacy regulations such as GDPR, especially regarding consent, data minimization, and user rights.

title: Unauthorized access to child search history
description: Unauthorized parties may access child search and watch history data stored in the MongoDB collection, potentially exposing sensitive information about children's viewing habits and interests.

title: Inadvertent disclosure of child watch history
description: Child watch history may be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized parties through system errors, misconfigured access controls, or data leakage during processing.

title: Loss of child profile data
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB may be lost due to system failures, corruption, or improper data management practices.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Storage and processing of child search and watch history may violate child privacy laws such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other regional child protection regulations.

title: Lack of control over child data access
description: There may be insufficient controls to ensure only authorized personnel can access child profile data, leading to potential privacy violations.

title: Unauthorized Video Disclosure During Upload
description: The parent user's video may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the upload process, potentially through insecure transmission channels or improper access controls.

title: Video Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The video may be disclosed to third parties or other users without proper authorization during the approval/rejection process.

title: Video Data Integrity During Processing
description: The video data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during transmission, storage, or processing by the Video Management Service.

title: Video Data Integrity During Approval
description: The video data may be modified during the approval/rejection process without proper audit trails or verification.

title: Lack of User Control Over Uploaded Video
description: The parent user may not have adequate control over how their video is processed, stored, or shared after upload, including inability to delete or revoke access.

title: Lack of Control Over Video Usage
description: The Video Management Service may not provide sufficient controls for the user to manage how their video is used, displayed, or distributed.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The video upload and approval process may not comply with applicable privacy laws and regulations such as GDPR or other data protection requirements.

title: Unintended Privacy Consequences
description: Uploading the video may have unintended privacy consequences for the user, such as the video being used for purposes other than intended or being shared with third parties without consent.

title: Non-Repudiation of Video Upload
description: There may be issues verifying that the parent user actually uploaded the video or that the approval/rejection was performed by the authorized person.

title: Unauthorized access to streamed video content
description: Video content may be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to the child user, potentially exposing inappropriate material or violating privacy expectations.

title: Inadequate controls over video content
description: The Video Management Service may not have sufficient controls to ensure only age-appropriate content is streamed to children, potentially violating child protection requirements.

title: Insufficient notification to child users
description: Child users may not be adequately informed about the nature and content of videos being streamed to them, reducing their ability to make informed decisions about their viewing.

title: Inappropriate video content for children
description: The video content streamed may not be age-appropriate or suitable for the child user, potentially causing harm or violating child protection policies.

title: Child data transfer may violate legal requirements
description: Transfer of child browsing data to AI engine may not comply with child privacy laws (COPPA, GDPR-K, etc.) which impose strict requirements for processing children's personal data.

title: Lack of parental consent for data processing
description: Children cannot provide meaningful consent; parental consent may not be obtained or documented for this planned data flow involving child browsing data.

title: Unintended disclosure of child browsing data
description: Child browsing data could be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized parties through the AI engine or during data transmission.

title: Excessive data collection for AI processing
description: May collect more child browsing data than necessary for the AI recommendation engine's intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: AI engine may leak or misuse child data
description: AI Recommendation Engine could potentially leak, misclassify, or misuse the child browsing data it receives, leading to unintended privacy violations.

title: Inadequate data destruction of child browsing data
description: Child browsing data may not be properly destroyed or anonymized after use by the AI engine, creating long-term privacy risks.

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or through security vulnerabilities, leading to potential identity theft or misuse of sensitive personal information.

title: Data loss or corruption of government ID images
description: Stored government ID images may be lost, corrupted, or become inaccessible due to file system failures, malware, or improper backup procedures, compromising the availability of critical authentication data.

title: Excessive data collection for authentication
description: Government ID images may contain more personal data than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy risk exposure.

title: Legal basis for storing government ID images unclear
description: The legal and legitimate basis for storing government ID images may not be clearly defined or documented, potentially violating privacy laws and regulatory requirements.

title: Insufficient notice about ID image storage
description: Users may not be adequately informed about how their government ID images are stored, retained, and potentially used beyond authentication purposes.

title: Unintended Disclosure of JWT via localStorage
description: JWT tokens stored in browser localStorage can be accessed by malicious scripts, browser extensions, or other users on the same device, leading to potential unauthorized access to authentication credentials.
assumptions: Assumes localStorage is accessible to all scripts on the page and potentially to other users on the same device.

title: Lack of Control over JWT Storage
description: Users have full control over localStorage (can clear, modify, or inspect it), but the authentication service has no control over what happens to the JWT once stored, including potential tampering or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes users may clear or modify localStorage without system intervention.

title: Data Destruction via localStorage Clearing
description: Users can clear localStorage, which would result in loss of JWT tokens, requiring re-authentication and potentially disrupting service.
assumptions: Assumes users may clear localStorage intentionally or accidentally.

title: Information Quality - JWT Compromise
description: JWT stored in localStorage may be compromised through XSS attacks or other means, leading to invalid or tampered authentication tokens.
assumptions: Assumes potential for XSS attacks or token manipulation.

title: Unauthorized access to child history data
description: Child history data could be accessed by unauthorized individuals during retrieval or transmission, potentially exposing sensitive information about minors.

title: Insecure transmission of child history data
description: Child history data may be transmitted without adequate encryption or confidentiality controls, risking exposure during data transfer.

title: Tampering with child history data
description: Child history data could be altered or corrupted during retrieval or storage, compromising data accuracy and integrity.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: The retrieval and sharing of child history data may not comply with applicable data protection regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K.

title: Inaccurate or incomplete child history data
description: Child history data retrieved may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, affecting the parent's ability to make informed decisions.

title: Parent accessing unauthorized child history data
description: Parent user may access child history data that they are not authorized to view, potentially violating privacy boundaries.
